_comment: Curated knowledge wells for collectors/knowledge.mjs — the authoritative, evergreen counterpart to social search. Each topic names the interest/boost it feeds (match), plus Wikipedia search terms, arXiv phrase queries, and curated YouTube channel_ids. Quality is by construction: you pick the wells, the ranker in CLAUDE.md still decides what's kept. Add a YouTube channel_id by opening youtube.com/@handle and copying the UC… from its RSS link (channel_id=UC…).

geoengineering.youtube_note: Simon Clark, Just Have a Think, DW Planet A, PBS Terra — climate-science channels; the ranker filters to genuinely SRM/geoengineering videos.

compute-ai-economics.youtube_note: Asianometry (@Asianometry) — semiconductors, chip supply chains, and the economics of compute; the ranker keeps the substantive fab/AI-hardware breakdowns.

prediction-markets.youtube_note: Patrick Boyle (@PBoyle) — former quant/hedge-fund manager; rigorous market-structure, liquidity, and derivatives explainers. The ranker filters to the microstructure/markets substance.

economics-explainers.match: Economics explainers / Marketing / Creator & platform economy
economics-explainers.youtube_note: Atrioc (@Atrioc) — 'Marketing Monday' business/econ & platform-economy breakdowns; the ranker filters to the substantive explainers, not the gaming VODs.

nuclear-energy.level_note: FUNDAMENTALS-FIRST (Swapnil, 2026-08-19: 'I need much simpler stuff — the very basics of the science; the arXiv was too much'). Serve the beginner ladder before any depth: what a nucleus/isotope is, what makes something radioactive, how fission releases energy, what a chain reaction is, and how a reactor turns that into electricity. Prefer the INTRO of a basic Wikipedia page (or a plain-English YouTube explainer) over a specialist page. NO arXiv — it is too advanced for where he is. Build up gradually across sweeps; only reach for neutronics/thermal-hydraulics/fuel-cycle detail once the basics are clearly landed.
nuclear-energy.youtube_note: Kyle Hill (accessible nuclear science communication — FIRST choice for the basics), T. Folse Nuclear (working nuclear-engineer explainers, still approachable), Improbable Matter (physics), Copenhagen Atomics (molten-salt R&D — more advanced). The ranker should now KEEP the clear beginner-friendly explainers and DROP anything that assumes prior reactor-physics knowledge — the opposite of the old 'keep the most technical' rule.
